questions.q: What problem does dynamic task mapping solve?
options: Creating a variable, run-time-known number of task instances instead of a hardcoded count
Making a DAG run faster regardless of task count
Removing the need for any dependencies between tasks
Automatically retrying every failed task forever
questions.explain: Dynamic task mapping handles cases where the number of tasks needed isn't known until run time, like processing however many files landed today.

options: Creates three separate task instances of add_one, each running with one element from the list
Runs add_one once with the entire list as a single argument
Deletes the add_one task and replaces it with three new tasks manually
Has no effect unless combined with a Sensor
questions.explain: expand() creates one task instance per list item — three items means three separate instances, each processing one element.

questions.q: What does 'Map Index' identify in the Grid view?
options: Which specific element in the list a particular mapped task instance processed
The total number of DAGs in the Airflow instance
The DAG's schedule interval
The worker machine a task ran on
questions.explain: Each mapped instance has its own Map Index (0, 1, 2, ...) corresponding to which list element it handled.

questions.q: In the map-then-reduce pattern, what does the 'reduce' task (like sum_it) receive?
options: The entire mapped output as a list, automatically, running just once
Nothing — reduce tasks never receive data from mapped tasks
Only the first mapped instance's result
A separate manual XCom push is required to pass the data
questions.explain: The reduce task runs once and automatically receives all the mapped results as a list — no manual wiring needed.

questions.q: If the list passed to .expand() has 20 items instead of 3, what happens?
options: 20 task instances are created automatically, with no code change needed
The task fails because it exceeds a hardcoded limit of 3
Only the first 3 items are processed
The DAG must be manually rewritten to add more task definitions
questions.explain: The number of task instances scales automatically with the list's length at run time — the code itself doesn't need to change.
